title: A single-cell transcriptome atlas reveals paradoxical monoallelic expression of RNA editing and heterozygous SNPs.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the only deposit this paper made, Figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.32952929, through the Figshare API: it holds one 9.2 MB zip of Sanger (capillary DNA sequencing) traces for one gene (FBgn0085437) across 38 samples. Searched the full text for any other deposit or code link and found none. Europe PMC's supplementary-files request timed out on its one attempt.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 13,025 Smart-Seq (full-length single-cell RNA sequencing) libraries reused from an earlier fly atlas, 7,930 cells passing a read filter, 32 samples, and the 94.0% / 92.8% binary-expression rates. All other inputs are raw SRA reads (SRR14470609/10, SRP273337, SRR8730642-44). No per-cell editing or SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) allele table appears to be deposited.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked Figshare: the only deposit is Sanger traces for one gene. The per-cell allele and editing calls are not deposited as far as the text shows. The supplement could not be retrieved.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Any label (for example, whether an editing site is monoallelic in a cell) would have to be built from raw reads by alignment, WASP remapping (a step that corrects reference-mapping bias) and variant calling. From the paper text.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are SRA accessions pointing to raw sequencing reads, which project rules forbid downloading.

a4_units_stated.note: No processed table exists to check.

a5_enough_rows.note: The paper reports 13,025 cells (7,930 after filtering). This count is from the text only and was not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 5.36 billion uniquely mapped reads (paper); raw FASTQ is likely hundreds of GB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Rebuilding the calls means realigning 13,025 libraries, which is not feasible on a laptop.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No processed file was available to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: The 'binary expression' pattern comes from a pipeline the authors themselves suspect reflects Smart-Seq artefacts (dropout, amplification bias), so it is not a clean physical measurement.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: no processed per-cell label table is deposited.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the sequence around a fly RNA editing site and the cell's type to predict whether only one copy of the gene is read out in that cell.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-cell, per-site records of editing or SNP allele reads from fly single-cell RNA sequencing; the number of rows is unknown because no such table is deposited.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a site shows reads from only one allele in a given cell. The calls would come from the authors' alignment and variant-calling pipeline run on Smart-Seq reads.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It could separate genuine one-copy expression from technical dropout in Smart-Seq data, which matters to labs that use single-cell data to study RNA editing.

ml_idea: Predict per-cell monoallelic editing or SNP expression from sequence context and cell type. This is blocked because the label exists only as raw reads processed by an undeposited pipeline.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: the processed table does not exist, and rebuilding it from raw reads is out of scope.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Get the NAR supplementary files and check whether any table lists per-cell editing or allele calls. The Figshare deposit has none.

verdict_reason: This is an analysis paper reusing raw Smart-Seq reads. Its only deposit (Figshare) is a 9 MB zip of Sanger traces for one gene, so there is no processed per-cell label table. Labels would have to be rebuilt from raw sequencing, which fails A1, A2, A3 and A6.
